model: Element-based redox thermochemistry with standard-state reaction rows

units.pressure: bar relative to 1 bar standard state

parent_registry.elemental_reference_state: Fe(cr) below 1809 K; Fe(l) at and above 1809 K

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF FeO liquid table, Fe-019; fitted row retained from the existing condensate database
provenance.selection_rationale: Direct assessed liquid function; reaction residual is at most 0.31 kJ/mol against the unshifted JANAF elemental fits over 1700-3000 K. The reaction band includes the Fe(l) fusion-anchor adjustment.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF O2 reference-state table, O-029
provenance.selection_rationale: Direct JANAF function; maximum local-node Gibbs residual is 0.00176 kJ/mol over the declared interval.

range_flags: JANAF Fe(cr) source nodes end at 1800 K; the fit is extended nine kelvin to the 1809 K transition marker.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF elemental iron crystal table, Fe-007
provenance.selection_rationale: Existing condensate φ fitter applied to JANAF H-H(298) and S nodes; the final nine kelvin to the transition marker is an explicitly flagged short extrapolation.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF elemental iron liquid table, Fe-006, Gibbs anchored continuously to the Fe(cr) fit at 1809 K
provenance.selection_rationale: Existing condensate φ fit is shifted by the 77.883 J/mol fusion-point offset so the crystal and liquid branches share one JANAF fusion Gibbs anchor; the 0.08 kJ/mol band covers the source-fit residual and anchor shift.

range_flags: The crystal fit uses source nodes through 1800 K; its endpoint is extended to the 1809 K transition marker.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF elemental iron tables Fe-007 and Fe-006
provenance.selection_rationale: Stable pure-iron reference state uses the crystal below the JANAF 1809 K fusion point and liquid at and above it; a_Fe is fixed to one for the saturation reference.

range_flags: 1500-1735 K is below the cited hematite decomposition marker and is a flagged supercooled metastable branch.
1735-1895 K is below nominal hypothetical fusion and remains a metastable extrapolation.
Lange and Navrotsky's tier-2 liquid-component Cp is extrapolated from its calorimetry domain across the 1500-3000 K runtime interval.
Fe2O3(l).band_method: conservative propagated Gibbs spread from the primary fusion-enthalpy estimate and tier-2 liquid-Cp uncertainty, sampled at 1500, 1895, 2195, 2695, and 3000 K

construction.fusion_temperature_status: nominal metastable hypothetical fusion; secondary transcription, primary estimate retained as an uncertainty bound

alternate_construction.source: Sugawara and Akaogi (2004), Calorimetry of liquids in the system Na2O-Fe2O3-SiO2; extrapolated hematite fusion estimate

construction.liquid_heat_capacity_method: tier 2 measured liquid-component Cp from Lange and Navrotsky (1992)
construction.liquid_heat_capacity_flag: amber; direct liquid-component measurement extrapolated beyond the calorimetry domain
construction.band_scope: conservative propagated fusion-enthalpy and tier-2 liquid-Cp uncertainty; the extrapolation remains a systematic limitation

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF hematite crystal table Fe-030; Lesher and Spera supplemental Table S5.5 secondary transcription, checked against Sugawara and Akaogi (2004)
provenance.selection_rationale: The central nominal fusion value follows the explicit Lesher and Spera secondary transcription; the genuine Sugawara and Akaogi primary estimate is retained as an uncertainty bound. The tier-2 liquid-component Cp is used centrally with its stated uncertainty and a high-temperature extrapolation flag; the hypothetical hematite phase remains metastable.

range_flags: The derived FeO1.5 standard state inherits the metastable and supercooled range of Fe2O3(l).

provenance.source: Half the constructed Fe2O3(l) standard Gibbs energy
provenance.selection_rationale: Stoichiometric pseudo-complex reference; it adds no independent Gibbs function.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF silicon liquid table Si-003
provenance.selection_rationale: Elemental standard fitted with the existing condensate φ fitter.

range_flags: JANAF liquid Cr is supercooled below its 2130 K crystal-liquid transition; 1700-2130 K is flagged.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF chromium liquid table Cr-003
provenance.selection_rationale: Elemental standard fitted with the existing condensate φ fitter.

range_flags: 1700-1728 K is below the 1728 K JANAF crystal-liquid transition and is flagged as supercooled liquid.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF nickel liquid table Ni-003
provenance.selection_rationale: Elemental standard fitted with the existing condensate φ fitter.

range_flags: 1700-1768 K is below the 1768 K JANAF beta-liquid transition and is flagged as supercooled liquid.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF cobalt liquid table Co-003
provenance.selection_rationale: Elemental standard fitted with the existing condensate φ fitter.

range_flags: Uses the JANAF liquid reference over 1600-2200 K, below the source table's 2334.526 K one-bar boiling marker.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF manganese liquid table Mn-003
provenance.selection_rationale: The existing condensate φ fitter was applied to the JANAF Mn(l) H-H(298), entropy, and heat-capacity nodes at 1600-2200 K; its maximum Gibbs residual is 0.000749 kJ/mol.

range_flags: Uses the existing NIST-JANAF Al-100 supercooled Al2O3 liquid reference over 1500-2000 K.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF Al-100 supercooled liquid function as packaged in the Al-100-SC-CP interval
provenance.selection_rationale: This is the existing Al2O3 liquid-component reference used over 1500-2000 K; its band uses the measured Tier 1 leave-one-out maximum at fusion.

range_flags: The constructed liquid is supercooled below the measured 2120 ± 20 K MnO melting point throughout this domain.
Fusion entropy and liquid heat capacity use Tier 3 systematic estimates with broad measured residual spreads.

provenance.source: IVTAN Table 1435 MnO crystal function with the measured MnO melting temperature; liquid function built with the tool's Tier 3 fusion-entropy and crystal-Cp estimates.
provenance.selection_rationale: The construction uses the measured crystal function and 2120 ± 20 K melting temperature. The tool's leave-one-out mean fusion entropy per formula atom supplies the center; IVTAN's 40 ± 5 kJ/mol fusion enthalpy is a cross-check only. Below fusion, the measured maximum input residuals use seven rock-salt monoxide homologues: BaO, CaO, FeO, MgO, SrO, TiO, and VO (N=7).

range_flags: Rhodonite melts incongruently; the pure-liquid standard is a constructed association reference.
The source heat-capacity fit is extended 64 K from its 1500 K upper limit to the selected 1564 K transition.

provenance.source: Robie, Huebner, and Hemingway rhodonite crystal thermochemistry; the 1559-1564 K interval is reported in the 2024 Mn-Si-O assessment.
provenance.selection_rationale: The crystal formation enthalpy and heat-capacity function are source-derived; the published ±2.0 kJ/mol formation-enthalpy uncertainty is counted once. The above-fusion recipe has no crystal-entropy uncertainty term. The liquid fusion entropy and Cp are Tier 3 systematic estimates. The leave-one-out Gibbs columns are interpolated to T-T_fus; the same residuals are not also added as propagated entropy and Cp spreads. No activity data were used to select the row.

range_flags: Tephroite is congruently melting only in the reported low-oxygen phase diagram; peritectic behavior is reported near air conditions.
The source heat-capacity fit is extended 16 K from its 1600 K upper limit to the selected 1616 K transition.

provenance.source: Robie et al. (1982) primary tephroite thermochemistry; the 1616-1620 K interval is reported in the 2024 Mn-Si-O assessment.
provenance.selection_rationale: The primary 1982 oxide-basis calorimetry reports ΔfH° = -1732.0 ± 2.9 kJ/mol; this value is used instead of the later -1731.5 tabulation. The transition interval comes from the 2024 Mn-Si-O assessment (Tier 3). The liquid fusion entropy and Cp are Tier 3 systematic estimates. Above fusion, the leave-one-out Gibbs columns are interpolated to T-T_fus and are not stacked with the same propagated entropy and Cp residuals.

range_flags: The constructed liquid is supercooled below the measured 2000 K peritectic throughout the runtime domain.
Heat capacity was measured on the crystal through 873 K and its published fit is extrapolated to the melting interval.

provenance.source: Open primary galaxite heat-capacity and entropy measurements by Navarro et al. (2012) and Navarro, de Avillez, Goes, and Gomes (2020), with primary phase-equilibrium data from Ilatovskaya and Fabrichnaya.
provenance.selection_rationale: The crystal Cp is taken from the primary DSC fit and extended from its measured range to the reported 2000 K peritectic; the low-temperature primary measurement gives S°298.15 = 118.7 ± 0.5 J/(mol K). No primary formation enthalpy is available: the center uses the -39.5 kJ/mol oxide-formation value used with the measured Cp in the Navarro assessment, with the published ±12.6 kJ/mol alternative carried once in the band. Below fusion, the Tier 3 entropy and Cp spreads use the maximum measured residuals among the two liquid-reference spinel homologues MgAl2O4 (Al-090) and Mg2TiO4 (Mg-032), N=2. Liquid fusion entropy and Cp centers use Tier 3 systematic estimates. Chen activities were not used to select the constants.

range_flags: Supercooled silica-liquid branch from the existing O-038-SC-CP construction.

provenance.source: Existing SiO2 supercooled liquid construction O-038-SC-CP
provenance.selection_rationale: Uses the existing supercooled branch below the direct liquid-function interval.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF silicon dioxide liquid table O-038
provenance.selection_rationale: Uses the direct assessed liquid function from its tabulated interval.

range_flags: Uses the existing supercooled silica construction below 1800 K and the direct JANAF liquid function at and above 1800 K.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF O-038 and its existing supercooled liquid construction
provenance.selection_rationale: The two existing standard-state branches meet within 0.01 kJ/mol at their 1800 K join.

rows.phase_or_construction: FeO(l) from JANAF; pure Fe uses crystal below and liquid at or above 1809 K.
rows.method: Assemble product-positive standard Gibbs terms with the existing condensate phi and JANAF Shomate evaluators.
rows.band_method: Maximum absolute reaction-Gibbs residual against the JANAF FeO formation-Gibbs values over 1700-3000 K.
rows.uncertainty_note: The 0.39 kJ/mol band includes the fitted reaction residual and the Fe(l) fusion-anchor adjustment; the Fe(cr) endpoint extrapolation is separately flagged.
range_flags: Fe metal switches from crystal to liquid at 1809 K; the crystal fit uses source nodes through 1800 K.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF FeO liquid table Fe-019 and elemental reference tables Fe-007, Fe-006, O-029
provenance.selection_rationale: Existing FeO parent row retained; the residual is at most 0.31 kJ/mol against unshifted JANAF elemental fits over 1700-3000 K, with the final reaction band including the Fe(l) fusion-anchor adjustment.

rows.phase_or_construction: FeO1.5(l) is one half Fe2O3(l), formed by the stated FeO oxidation reaction; Fe2O3(l) is a hypothetical metastable fusion construction.
rows.method: Assemble product-positive standard Gibbs terms with the existing condensate phi and JANAF Shomate evaluators.
rows.band_method: Conservative sum of one half the propagated Fe2O3 fusion-enthalpy and tier-2 liquid-Cp band, the FeO reaction band, and one quarter the O2 fit band.
rows.uncertainty_note: The band includes the primary fusion-estimate bound and stated tier-2 Cp uncertainty; high-temperature Cp extrapolation and hypothetical hematite metastability remain flagged.
range_flags: FeO1.5 uses half the hypothetical metastable Fe2O3(l) construction.
1500-1735 K is below the cited hematite decomposition marker and is a flagged supercooled metastable branch.
1735-1895 K is below nominal hypothetical fusion and remains a metastable extrapolation.
Lange and Navrotsky's tier-2 liquid-component Cp is extrapolated across the 1500-3000 K runtime interval.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF Fe-030 hematite crystal, Lesher and Spera supplemental Table S5.5, Sugawara and Akaogi (2004), and Lange and Navrotsky (1992)
provenance.selection_rationale: Reaction stoichiometry fixes the pseudo-complex; the centrally selected secondary fusion transcription is bounded by the verified primary estimate, and the tier-2 liquid-component Cp is central with stated uncertainty and an extrapolation flag.

rows.phase_or_construction: Pure liquid MnO at 1 bar from the measured MnO crystal function and a Tier 3 systematic fusion construction.
rows.method: Assemble product-positive standard Gibbs terms with the existing condensate phi and JANAF Shomate evaluators.
rows.band_method: Conservative sum of the below-fusion MnO construction band using the seven-rock-salt-monoxide maximum residuals, the Mn(l) source-fit band, and one half the O2 fit band.
rows.uncertainty_note: The MnO liquid reference is supercooled throughout the declared domain; the below-fusion band uses domain-matched measured monoxide residuals and the measured leave-one-out anchor.
range_flags: MnO(l) is supercooled below its measured 2120 ± 20 K melting point throughout 1673-2000 K.
The fusion entropy and liquid heat capacity are systematic estimates rather than direct liquid measurements.

provenance.source: NIST-JANAF Mn(l) table Mn-003 and IVTAN Table 1435 MnO crystal function
provenance.selection_rationale: The elemental reference uses the direct assessed liquid-metal function; the oxide uses the measured melting point and crystal function with a tool-derived Tier 3 center. IVTAN's estimated fusion enthalpy is a cross-check only.

rows.phase_or_construction: Rhodonite-derived liquid association reference; the rhodonite crystal melts incongruently and the liquid standard is constructed.
rows.method: Assemble product-positive standard Gibbs terms with the existing condensate phi evaluator and the existing piecewise silica reference.
rows.band_method: Sum of the MnSiO3(l) band from interpolated Tier 3 leave-one-out columns, its independent fusion-temperature interval and fit residual, the MnO(l) band, and the SiO2(l) band.
rows.uncertainty_note: The leave-one-out columns are interpolated to T-T_fus; the same residuals are not also stacked as propagated entropy and heat-capacity spreads. The Chen activity data remain held out.
range_flags: Rhodonite melts incongruently; MnSiO3(l) is an association standard constructed from open crystal thermochemistry.
The source heat-capacity fit is extended from 1500 K to the selected 1564 K transition.

provenance.source: Robie, Huebner, and Hemingway rhodonite crystal thermochemistry; transition interval from the 2024 Mn-Si-O assessment
provenance.selection_rationale: The reaction is fixed by crystal stoichiometry. The 1559-1564 K transition interval is taken from https://doi.org/10.1007/s00269-024-01302-8 (Tier 3). The liquid Gibbs function is constructed from the crystal function and systematic fusion estimates; no activity data selected its parameters.

rows.phase_or_construction: Tephroite-derived liquid association reference; its phase behavior near air is peritectic and the liquid standard is constructed.
rows.method: Assemble product-positive standard Gibbs terms with the existing condensate phi evaluator and the existing piecewise silica reference.
rows.band_method: Sum of the Mn2SiO4(l) band from interpolated Tier 3 leave-one-out columns, its independent source enthalpy and fusion-temperature uncertainties and fit residual, two MnO(l) bands, and the SiO2(l) band.
rows.uncertainty_note: The leave-one-out columns are interpolated to T-T_fus; the same residuals are not also stacked as propagated entropy and heat-capacity spreads. The primary tephroite enthalpy uncertainty is counted once. The Chen activity data remain held out.
range_flags: Tephroite peritectic behavior is reported near air conditions; Mn2SiO4(l) is an association standard constructed from open crystal thermochemistry.
The source heat-capacity fit is extended from 1600 K to the selected 1616 K transition.

provenance.source: Robie et al. (1982) primary tephroite thermochemistry; transition interval from the 2024 Mn-Si-O assessment
provenance.selection_rationale: The primary oxide-basis calorimetry reports ΔfH° = -1732.0 ± 2.9 kJ/mol; the later -1731.5 tabulation is not used. The 1616-1620 K interval is from https://doi.org/10.1007/s00269-024-01302-8 (Tier 3). The liquid standard is constructed from the crystal function and systematic fusion estimates; no activity data selected its parameters.

rows.phase_or_construction: Galaxite-derived liquid association reference from open primary crystal thermochemistry; the liquid standard is constructed below its peritectic interval.
rows.method: Assemble product-positive standard Gibbs terms with the existing condensate phi evaluator.
rows.band_method: Sum of the constructed galaxite band, including its crystal formation-enthalpy and entropy uncertainties, the MnO(l) band, and the existing Al2O3(l) supercooled-reference band.
rows.uncertainty_note: The heat-capacity fit is extrapolated above its measured range and the formation enthalpy is assessed rather than directly measured. Chen activity data were held out and did not select the equilibrium constant.
range_flags: Galaxite melts peritectically near 2000 K; the liquid association standard is constructed from crystal data.
The primary DSC heat-capacity fit is measured through 873 K and extrapolated to the melting interval.

provenance.source: Navarro et al. (2012) and Navarro, de Avillez, Goes, and Gomes (2020) primary galaxite heat-capacity and entropy measurements, plus Ilatovskaya and Fabrichnaya primary phase-equilibrium measurements
provenance.selection_rationale: Galaxite is included from open primary crystal thermochemistry. Its Gibbs function uses the measured Cp fit and S°298.15; no primary formation enthalpy exists, so the assessed -39.5 kJ/mol oxide-formation value is used with ±12.6 kJ/mol uncertainty. Below fusion, the Tier 3 entropy and Cp spreads use the maximum measured residuals among the two liquid-reference spinel homologues MgAl2O4 (Al-090) and Mg2TiO4 (Mg-032), N=2. No Chen activity data were used to choose the row. Held-out summary: all_three: median ratio 5.809, out-of-band 55/55; without_MnSiO3: median ratio 9.583, out-of-band 55/55; without_Mn2SiO4: median ratio 6.205, out-of-band 55/55; without_MnAl2O4: median ratio 7.261, out-of-band 55/55; MnSiO3_only: median ratio 7.692, out-of-band 55/55; Mn2SiO4_only: median ratio 14.926, out-of-band 55/55; MnAl2O4_only: median ratio 11.487, out-of-band 55/55; no_complexes: median ratio 18.058, out-of-band 55/55. These comparisons use the held-out Chen datasets after MnO solid-to-liquid reference conversion; no equilibrium constant was tuned to them.
